Demand for loans is driven mainly by macroeconomic conditions, interest rates, and capital availability rather than processing cost or speed, so 10x productivity gains unlock only modest extra volume (e.g., marginal borrowers or faster turnaround) rather than large expansion. High disruption combined with low elasticity therefore points to net headcount contraction as AI absorbs the bulk of evaluation work.

title: Lodging managers
rationale: Core duties center on on-site presence—inspecting rooms and grounds, resolving guest and staff issues in real time, hiring/training, and leadership—which AI can only peripherally assist via revenue tools, scheduling software, or chatbots; the physical and interpersonal core keeps disruption moderate. Demand for lodging managers is largely fixed by the stock of properties and travel volumes rather than management cost, so even large productivity gains mainly allow leaner staffing per facility rather than unlocking dramatically more hotels or manager roles. Because disruption stays at or below the moderate threshold, the occupation remains resilient overall, with AI reshaping tools but not the fundamental need for human managers on property.

title: Logging workers
rationale: Core tasks center on physical outdoor work—operating chain saws and heavy machinery in unpredictable forest terrain, felling, skidding, loading, and basic equipment maintenance—which AI and robotics can only peripherally assist via planning tools, computer-vision grading, or limited semi-autonomy over the next decade. Demand for timber is largely fixed by construction, manufacturing, and environmental constraints rather than logging cost or speed, so productivity gains (already visible from mechanization) translate into fewer workers rather than expanded output. Because disruption remains low-to-moderate, the occupation is resilient: AI touches admin and optimization edges without reshaping the hands-on core.

title: Logisticians
rationale: Core duties such as demand forecasting, inventory optimization, risk monitoring, system selection, and strategy proposals are predominantly cognitive and data-driven, already being materially advanced by AI/ML tools in supply-chain platforms, producing high disruption. Elasticity is high because e-commerce volume, multi-tier global networks, and resilience requirements create large latent demand; cheaper, faster logistics analysis lets more firms and more product lines receive sophisticated coordination. Consequently productivity gains expand total work rather than shrink headcount, placing the occupation in the augment category.

title: Machinists and tool and die makers
rationale: Core work mixes physical machine setup, material handling, real-time monitoring, manual adjustments, and precision verification on the shop floor with digital elements like CAD/CAM interpretation and CNC programming; AI already assists toolpath optimization, simulation, and inspection but cannot eliminate the need for human presence and dexterity in unpredictable manufacturing environments. Demand for precision metal parts and dies is constrained by end-product markets, material costs, and overall manufacturing volume, so large productivity gains primarily raise efficiency rather than unlocking dramatically higher total output. Because disruption remains moderate, the occupation is resilient: AI reshapes peripheral knowledge tasks and boosts output per worker without displacing the hands-on core.

title: Management analysts
rationale: Core tasks center on data gathering, financial and operational analysis, solution design, report writing, and presentations—predominantly cognitive and language-based work where AI tools already accelerate research, synthesis, modeling, and drafting. Onsite interviews, client relationship management, and change implementation still require human presence, keeping disruption high rather than near-total. Demand is highly elastic because consulting spend is currently constrained by high cost and limited capacity; dramatically cheaper and faster analysis unlocks continuous optimization for smaller firms, governments, and more frequent engagements across industries. Productivity gains therefore expand total output and headcount rather than pure substitution, fitting the augment category.

title: Manicurists and pedicurists
rationale: Core tasks—trimming, filing, massaging, applying polish or artificial nails, and disinfecting tools—are almost entirely physical, dexterous, and client-present, so AI has negligible impact beyond peripheral admin, booking, or design-suggestion tools. Demand elasticity is moderate because lower cost and faster service would unlock more frequent visits, mini-sessions, and uptake among men or lower-income clients, yet total consumption remains bounded by personal time and preference rather than exploding. With disruption well below the threshold that reshapes the occupation, the net effect is resilient: AI touches the edges while the hands-on service model and employment trajectory stay intact.

title: Marine engineers and naval architects
rationale: Core work is predominantly knowledge-based—CAD layouts, hull/superstructure design, fluid/performance analysis, cost estimates, and technical reports—which AI already accelerates via generative design, simulation, and automated drafting, though physical prototype testing, shipyard oversight, and regulatory coordination keep it from higher scores. Demand elasticity is only moderate because the number of vessels, offshore platforms, and coastal structures is constrained by capital costs, global trade/military needs, and shipyard capacity rather than design labor; cheaper design unlocks more emissions-compliant redesigns and wind projects but not order-of-magnitude volume growth. High disruption plus moderate elasticity therefore produces restructure: the occupation persists but shifts toward AI-orchestrated design validation, novel problem-solving, and field integration.

title: Market research analysts
rationale: Core tasks—statistical analysis of consumer and competitor data, forecasting trends, generating charts/reports, and synthesizing insights—are almost entirely digital and cognitive, already being materially accelerated by LLMs, automated analytics platforms, and generative tools for survey design and visualization. Physical or in-person elements (focus groups, client presentations) are secondary and shrinking as secondary data and digital methods dominate. Demand is highly elastic because thorough market research has historically been cost-prohibitive for many firms and product iterations; 10x cheaper/faster output unlocks continuous monitoring, more A/B testing, deeper segmentation, and research by smaller businesses that previously skipped it. Productivity gains therefore expand total volume of research rather than simply shrinking headcount, allowing skilled analysts who leverage AI to produce far more value.

title: Marriage and family therapists
rationale: Core duties revolve around real-time interpersonal assessment, building therapeutic rapport, and guiding emotional processing in couples/families—tasks that demand human empathy, non-verbal attunement, and adaptive presence that AI cannot fully replace, even as tools already assist with notes, treatment-plan drafting, and admin. Demand is highly elastic because access to relationship and family therapy is currently constrained by cost, waitlists, and shortages; cheaper/faster delivery would unlock substantial latent need across underserved populations. Moderate disruption therefore keeps the occupation resilient, with AI enhancing productivity without reshaping the human-centered core.

title: Masonry workers
rationale: Core masonry tasks—cutting and laying brick/block/stone, mixing and spreading mortar, aligning structures with levels, and finishing surfaces—are almost entirely physical, manual, and site-based, requiring strength, dexterity, and real-world presence that AI cannot perform. AI may assist only peripherally with blueprint reading, material estimates, or scheduling, leaving the occupation largely unchanged. Demand for masonry is constrained by overall construction volume, building codes, material costs, and economic cycles rather than labor price alone, so even large productivity gains would produce only limited expansion in total output. With disruption well below the threshold for transformation, the occupation remains resilient.

title: Massage therapists
rationale: Core tasks center on hands-on physical manipulation of soft tissues, joint mobilization, and real-time tactile evaluation, all requiring human presence, strength, and dexterity that current or near-term AI cannot perform. AI can only assist peripheral elements such as client intake notes, scheduling, marketing, and basic treatment suggestions. Demand for massage is moderately elastic—lower effective costs could unlock more frequent wellness and pain-management sessions—but physical stamina limits, client preference for human touch, and the discretionary nature of the service cap expansion. Low disruption therefore places the occupation firmly in the resilient category regardless of modest demand growth.

title: Material moving machine operators
rationale: Core tasks center on physical control of forklifts, cranes, and conveyors in dynamic real-world settings that demand coordination, visual judgment, and on-site presence, so AI mainly aids peripheral elements such as sensor-based tracking, route planning, and digital records rather than the hands-on operation itself. Over ten years autonomous systems and AI safety assists will raise efficiency in structured warehouses, yet unstructured sites, safety rules, and equipment complexity keep full displacement limited, producing only moderate disruption. Material-moving volume expands somewhat with cheaper logistics and e-commerce, but regulatory, spatial, and capital constraints prevent demand from scaling enough to offset productivity gains, so headcount remains largely inelastic. Because disruption stays moderate, the occupation is resilient overall.

title: Material recording clerks
rationale: Core tasks center on digital recordkeeping, inventory tracking via RFID/sensors, report compilation, scheduling, and accuracy checks—all highly amenable to AI automation, computer vision for defect inspection, and predictive systems, even as residual physical handling of packages remains; AI tools already materially reshape the workflow and will deepen this over the decade. Demand for material recording is largely derived from fixed goods volume in manufacturing, retail, and logistics rather than suppressed by cost, so 10x productivity gains translate primarily into fewer clerks needed rather than dramatically more tracking or shipping activity. This matches the replace category because high disruption meets low elasticity, consistent with BLS projections of employment decline from automation and RFID/robots.

title: Materials engineers
rationale: Materials engineers' core work is predominantly knowledge-based—computational modeling of atomic structures, property prediction via software and ML, materials selection/optimization, failure analysis, and technical reporting—where AI tools for simulation, generative design, and data analysis are already materially useful and advancing rapidly, even as physical lab testing and factory oversight persist. Demand elasticity is high because materials R&D is currently slow and expensive, suppressing exploration of vast candidate spaces; 10x cheaper/faster discovery would unlock far more alloys, polymers, semiconductors, and composites for aerospace, energy, electronics, and sustainability applications. This combination of high disruption with high elasticity means productivity gains expand total output and innovation rather than contracting headcount, fitting the augment category.

title: Mathematicians and statisticians
rationale: Core tasks—model development, statistical coding, data analysis, experiment design, and interpretation—are almost entirely digital/cognitive and already heavily assisted by AI tools for code generation, AutoML, visualization, and reasoning, placing them squarely in AI’s path. Demand elasticity is high because the volume of data and decision problems far exceeds current analytical capacity; making rigorous modeling 10x cheaper unlocks far more A/B tests, clinical designs, risk models, and scientific analyses across business, healthcare, and government. Productivity gains are therefore absorbed by expanded output rather than headcount cuts, so the occupation is augmented: workers who master AI tools produce dramatically more while overall employment continues to grow.

title: Mechanical engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Core duties mix digital/cognitive work (3D CAD layouts, design evaluation, data analysis, calculations, and recommendations) with substantial physical/manual tasks (assembling parts, setting up and conducting tests, installing, troubleshooting, and operating machinery), so AI already assists design and analysis tools but cannot replace hands-on presence or real-world testing. Elasticity is moderate because cheaper/faster design and iteration would unlock some additional product development and manufacturing support, yet demand remains constrained by physical production capacity, materials, and end-market absorption for mechanical goods. With disruption only moderate, AI reshapes peripheral knowledge tasks without transforming the occupation's essential hands-on character, fitting the resilient category.

title: Mechanical engineers
rationale: Mechanical engineering is predominantly knowledge work centered on analysis, CAD design, simulation, and optimization—tasks where AI tools already deliver material gains via generative design, automated FEA, and predictive modeling—while physical prototyping and site oversight remain secondary. Demand elasticity is high because dramatically cheaper and faster design cycles unlock latent needs for more product variants, custom machinery, robotics integration, energy systems, and automation projects that were previously cost-prohibitive. Productivity gains therefore expand total engineering output across manufacturing, transportation, and R&D rather than contracting headcount. The combination produces augmentation: engineers who master AI produce far more sophisticated systems and the occupation grows.

title: Medical and health services managers
rationale: Core duties center on knowledge work—budgeting, compliance monitoring, goal-setting, analytics, scheduling, and reporting—that AI tools already assist and will increasingly automate or accelerate via predictive staffing models, automated EHR analysis, and regulatory scanning, substantially reshaping daily tasks. Leadership, interpersonal staff supervision, on-site crisis response, and high-stakes regulatory judgment still require human presence, preventing full automation. Elasticity is moderate because aging-driven healthcare expansion and rising system complexity create room for more managed facilities and services when management becomes cheaper, yet demand remains partly constrained by physical infrastructure, licensing, and staffing ratios rather than pure cost, so productivity gains produce skill shifts more than pure headcount growth.

title: Medical assistants
rationale: Disruption is moderate because core clinical duties (taking vitals, assisting exams, injections, specimen collection) require physical presence and patient interaction that AI cannot replace, while administrative tasks (scheduling, EHR entry, coding, inventory) are already being assisted by AI tools. Elasticity is moderate as aging demographics and unmet care needs create some room for expanded throughput if MAs become more productive, yet facility capacity, physician supply, and regulatory limits constrain how much total demand can grow. The net effect is resilient since AI mainly augments peripheral admin work without reshaping the hands-on core of the occupation.

title: Medical dosimetrists
rationale: Core work is almost entirely digital and computational—reviewing CT/MRI scans, optimizing radiation dose distributions, and designing delivery plans via specialized software—placing it squarely in AI’s path; existing auto-contouring, inverse-planning, and ML-based TPS tools already materially accelerate these tasks and will continue to do so. Demand for treatment plans is tightly coupled to the fixed incidence of radiotherapy-eligible cancers and the number of available linear accelerators, so a 10x productivity gain does not unlock proportional new volume. Regulatory oversight, liability, and the clinical bottleneck of patient throughput further limit expansion, producing headcount contraction rather than offsetting growth.

title: Medical equipment repairers
rationale: Core work centers on physical installation, hands-on diagnosis with tools, mechanical/electronic repairs, calibration, and on-site presence around patients and heavy equipment, so AI mainly assists peripheral tasks like predictive maintenance software, remote diagnostics, record-keeping, and software updates rather than displacing the manual core. Demand elasticity is moderate because healthcare volume and equipment proliferation (driven by aging populations and chronic disease) create some expansion if repairs become cheaper and faster, enabling broader deployment and better upkeep, yet structural limits from facility capacity and regulation prevent unlimited growth. With disruption only moderate, the occupation remains resilient as AI does not reshape the essential in-person technical work.

title: Medical records specialists
rationale: Core work is almost entirely digital and cognitive—reviewing clinical documentation, assigning ICD/CPT codes, EHR data entry, and accuracy checks—all of which current NLP and AI coding tools already perform or assist at high accuracy, with rapid further gains expected. Demand for these services is tightly coupled to the fixed volume of patient encounters and billing events rather than to the cost or speed of coding itself; cheaper processing does not generate meaningfully more healthcare utilization or records. High disruption combined with low elasticity therefore points to substantial headcount contraction as AI absorbs the bulk of the workload.

title: Medical scientists
rationale: Medical scientists perform predominantly knowledge-work tasks—hypothesis generation, study design, data analysis from trials and samples, grant writing, and publication—where AI already accelerates literature synthesis, bioinformatics, experimental design, and even molecular discovery, with rapid further gains expected; physical lab handling, clinical oversight, and high-stakes judgment keep it from the highest tier. Demand elasticity is high because society has vast unmet needs for treatments of aging-related, chronic, and emerging diseases; 10x cheaper/faster research would unlock far more trials, drug candidates, and personalized studies rather than simply shrinking headcount. The combination therefore produces augmentation: each scientist becomes dramatically more productive while total research output and employment expand.

title: Medical transcriptionists
rationale: Core tasks—listening to medical dictation, converting speech to structured reports, editing speech-recognition drafts for accuracy, and applying medical terminology—are almost entirely digital, language-based, and cognitive, placing them squarely in the path of advancing AI speech-to-text and NLP systems that already produce usable drafts and are rapidly improving. Demand for transcription is inelastic because the volume of reports is fixed by the number of patient encounters and clinical documentation requirements; making the process 10x cheaper or faster does not generate more medical visits or more reports. Consequently, productivity gains translate directly into fewer workers needed, matching the BLS projection of employment decline and fitting the replace category.

title: Meeting, convention, and event planners
rationale: Disruption is moderate-to-high because a large share of the work—client scoping, venue research and bidding, budgeting, vendor coordination, and post-event analysis—is cognitive, language-based, and already assisted by AI tools for proposals, optimization, and communications, yet core duties still require physical venue inspection, on-site real-time problem-solving, and interpersonal relationship management that AI cannot fully absorb. Elasticity is moderate because dramatically cheaper planning would unlock more professional help for personal events (weddings, reunions) and more frequent smaller corporate or hybrid gatherings, but overall demand remains constrained by venue capacity, attendee time, and the dominant non-planning costs of events themselves. With disruption at the upper edge of the moderate range, the occupation is resilient: AI will reshape tools and peripheral workflows without displacing the human-centric core of event orchestration.

title: Metal and plastic machine workers
rationale: Core tasks mix physical machine setup, material handling, tool changes, and on-floor monitoring with cognitive elements like blueprint interpretation, CNC programming, parameter adjustment, and inspection; AI already aids via computer vision QC, predictive maintenance, toolpath optimization, and code generation, but unpredictable real-world machine intervention and factory presence keep disruption moderate rather than high. Demand for the parts produced expands only modestly if costs fall, constrained by end-market saturation for goods, material costs, and global competition, so productivity gains historically and prospectively shrink headcount rather than unlock large latent volume. With disruption at or below 6, the occupation remains resilient overall even as automation continues the projected employment decline.

title: Microbiologists
rationale: Core tasks mix physical lab work (culturing, experiments, equipment use) with heavy cognitive components (experimental design, microbial identification/classification via imaging or sequencing data, statistical analysis, grant writing, and technical reporting); AI already materially accelerates the latter through image recognition, genomic ML models, literature synthesis, and protocol optimization, and will deepen this over 10 years even as wet-lab presence remains. Demand elasticity is high because cheaper, faster microbial research and testing unlocks substantial latent applications in drug discovery, synthetic biology, industrial fermentation, biofuels, environmental remediation, and public-health surveillance that are currently constrained by cost and throughput. The combination produces an augment outcome: each microbiologist becomes dramatically more productive while total output and employment expand rather than contract.

title: Middle school teachers
rationale: AI already materially alters core cognitive tasks such as lesson planning, content creation, grading, assessment design, and differentiation, so disruption is high even though real-time classroom management, adolescent social-emotional support, and physical supervision still require human presence. Demand elasticity is only moderate because the student population is demographically fixed and schooling is compulsory, yet cheaper/faster teaching can unlock latent demand for smaller classes, more specialized or enrichment offerings, and higher-quality individualized support within existing budgets. The combination produces restructuring: the occupation persists but the skill mix shifts heavily toward AI orchestration, facilitation, and relationship work, displacing those who do not adapt.

title: Military careers
rationale: Military careers span a wide mix of roles, from combat specialties and transportation that demand physical presence, fitness, and real-time judgment in unpredictable hostile environments, to technical, intelligence, logistics, and administrative work where AI already assists with analysis, simulation, predictive maintenance, and planning; overall this yields only moderate disruption as core missions still require human leadership, accountability, and boots-on-the-ground capability. Demand elasticity is low because force size is set by geopolitics, threat assessments, and congressional end-strength authorizations rather than market price or productivity; AI force-multipliers (autonomous systems, better ISR) are more likely to enable smaller or differently composed units than to expand total personnel demand. The combination of moderate disruption and inelastic demand places the occupation firmly in the resilient category.

title: Mining and geological engineers
rationale: Core work mixes high-end knowledge tasks (mine design, geological modeling, optimization, technical reporting, production analysis) that AI already accelerates via simulation, generative design, and sensor analytics with irreducible on-site supervision, safety inspections, and physical construction oversight in remote environments, placing disruption in the high but not extreme range. Demand for mining engineering services is constrained by commodity prices, capital intensity of mines, environmental permitting, and geology rather than engineering cost or speed, so 10x productivity gains unlock only limited additional exploration or reclamation work. Because disruption sits at the upper edge of the moderate-to-high band, the occupation remains resilient: AI reshapes analytical tools and workflows but does not eliminate the need for human engineers on the ground.

title: Models
rationale: Core commercial tasks such as posing for print/online ads, product catalogs, and digital campaigns are already being substantially displaced by generative AI image/video tools that create photorealistic virtual models, composites, and infinite variations without a human subject, while runway, fitting, and live event work remain physical but represent a smaller share. Demand elasticity is low because the need for actual human models is constrained by the finite number of physical fashion shows, trade events, and brand campaigns that specifically require real people; expanded digital content volume is absorbed by AI rather than more human bookings. High disruption combined with low elasticity therefore produces net replacement and headcount contraction, matching the BLS outlook that AI image reuse and digital alternatives will limit employment.

title: Music directors and composers
rationale: Core tasks blend highly AI-vulnerable cognitive work (composing, arranging, score interpretation and selection—already transformed by generative tools like Suno/AIVA and notation software) with human-presence leadership (live rehearsals, conducting, auditions, and interpersonal direction of ensembles). This yields high disruption as AI materially reshapes the creative pipeline even if live conducting remains human. Elasticity is moderate because cheaper/faster composition unlocks more media, game, ad, and indie scores, yet live directing demand stays constrained by fixed institutional needs (churches, orchestras), arts funding, and audience capacity. The occupation therefore restructures around AI collaboration and distinctive human leadership rather than pure replacement or pure expansion.

title: Musicians and singers
rationale: Core tasks center on live performance, physical instrument playing or singing, rehearsals, and real-time audience interaction that require human presence, musical talent, and stamina; AI already assists composition, studio production, practice feedback, and social-media promotion but leaves the performative core intact, producing only moderate disruption. Elasticity is moderate because dramatically cheaper/faster output would expand use of music in media, advertising, games, and more frequent local/private events, yet overall demand remains constrained by finite audience attention, venue capacity, and time. With disruption only moderate, the occupation is resilient: AI tools augment peripheral and creative-support work without reshaping the fundamental human performance role.

title: Natural sciences managers
rationale: Core duties center on cognitive and language-based knowledge work—setting research strategies, budgeting, reviewing scientific output, drafting reports, and providing technical guidance—which AI already assists via analysis, summarization, project tools, and decision support, even as interpersonal leadership, hiring, and lab/field presence remain human. This places the role in the high-disruption band shared with other managers. Elasticity is moderate because cheaper, faster management can unlock additional R&D projects and larger supervised teams in expanding fields like biotech, yet overall demand remains constrained by research funding, regulatory limits, and the flexibility of span-of-control, so productivity gains only partially expand headcount. The combination of high disruption and moderate elasticity therefore produces restructuring: the occupation persists but requires substantial skill shifts toward AI orchestration and higher-level scientific judgment.

title: Network and computer systems administrators
rationale: Core tasks center on digital configuration, monitoring, security, performance optimization, scripting, and remote troubleshooting of networks and systems—areas where AI tools (AIOps, automated remediation, log analysis, config generation) already materially accelerate work and will deepen further, even if occasional hardware installs remain. Demand is inelastic because organizations need a relatively fixed quantum of reliable infrastructure rather than 10x more administration; cheaper/faster delivery simply consolidates headcount via automation, DevOps absorption, and Networks-as-a-Service, consistent with the projected employment decline. High disruption combined with low elasticity therefore produces net replacement of roles.

title: News analysts, reporters, and journalists
rationale: Core tasks such as researching topics, writing and updating stories, analyzing information, scripting for broadcast, and reviewing for accuracy/style are predominantly cognitive and language-based knowledge work where AI tools already draft content, summarize sources, assist fact-checking, and speed multimedia production; human elements like in-person interviews, source relationships, and on-location reporting remain but are increasingly AI-augmented. Demand elasticity is low because news consumption is constrained by finite audience attention and existing free abundance rather than production cost or speed, so 10x cheaper output does not unlock dramatically more reading/viewing or new markets sufficient to offset productivity gains. Structural factors like ad-revenue decline and media consolidation further cap expansion. High disruption paired with low elasticity therefore implies AI absorbs substantial core work without compensatory demand growth, producing net headcount contraction.

title: Nuclear engineers
rationale: Core tasks center on cognitive work—reactor and shielding design, radiation transport simulations, safety analysis, procedure writing, and regulatory compliance review—which are already materially assisted by computational tools and will be further accelerated by AI generative design, optimization, and data analysis; physical plant presence and ultimate human accountability for safety-critical decisions prevent full automation. Demand elasticity is moderate because cheaper, faster engineering can unlock more advanced-reactor concepts, medical-isotope work, and space applications in some segments, yet overall headcount growth remains capped by capital costs, licensing timelines, and policy constraints on nuclear deployment. High disruption paired with only moderate elasticity therefore implies the occupation persists but requires substantial skill shifts toward AI orchestration, systems judgment, and regulatory expertise.

title: Nuclear medicine technologists
rationale: Core work centers on physical patient handling, precise preparation and injection of radiopharmaceuticals, real-time operation of specialized scanners, and radiation safety protocols that require on-site presence and cannot be fully digitized; AI can assist with dosage calculations, image optimization, and records but leaves the majority of daily tasks intact. Demand for nuclear medicine procedures is driven by clinical necessity, aging demographics, and strict radiation-exposure limits rather than price or speed, so even large productivity gains would not unlock large volumes of additional scans. Because disruption remains moderate, the occupation falls into the resilient category regardless of elasticity.

title: Nuclear technicians
rationale: Core duties center on physical presence in plants and labs—calibrating and maintaining radiation equipment, collecting environmental samples, onsite incident response, and hands-on mechanical work under strict safety protocols—so AI can only assist peripheral data analysis, sensor interpretation, and calculations rather than reshape the occupation. Demand is tightly constrained by the fixed number of nuclear facilities, regulatory staffing minima, and capital/policy decisions around power generation, not by technician labor cost or speed; cheaper monitoring therefore yields headcount reduction rather than expanded output. Because disruption remains moderate, the occupation stays resilient overall even as AI tools improve efficiency at the margins.

title: Nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, and nurse practitioners
rationale: Core duties center on physical exams, hands-on procedures (anesthesia administration, labor and delivery, monitoring equipment), real-time patient observation, and in-person counseling that require unpredictable physical presence, so AI only assists peripheral cognitive elements such as history analysis, diagnostic suggestions, and care-plan drafting. Demand is highly elastic because primary and specialty care access is currently constrained by provider shortages, cost, and geography; productivity gains would unlock substantial latent utilization from aging populations, chronic disease management, and underserved markets rather than simply reducing headcount. With disruption only moderate, the occupation remains resilient: AI tools will raise individual productivity without displacing the essential human clinical role.

title: Nursing assistants and orderlies
rationale: Core tasks such as bathing, toileting, transferring, feeding, and transporting patients are almost entirely physical and require unpredictable real-world human presence, so AI only touches peripheral elements like automated vital-sign devices or documentation; this keeps disruption low. Elasticity is moderate because an aging population and chronic understaffing create some latent demand for more hours of care or expanded home/community services if costs fall, yet the fundamental volume of patients needing basic assistance remains relatively fixed by demographics and clinical need. The combination places the occupation firmly in the resilient category, as AI does not reshape the hands-on core of the work.

title: Occupational health and safety specialists and technicians
rationale: Core work mixes physical on-site inspections, equipment testing, and fieldwork in factories/construction with cognitive tasks like risk analysis, program design, incident investigation, and report writing; AI already assists the latter via data analytics, predictive modeling, and automated reporting but cannot replace human presence, judgment, or PPE-required site work, keeping disruption moderate. Demand is driven largely by regulations and fixed numbers of workplaces, yet cheaper/faster services would unlock some expansion via more proactive consulting, small-business adoption, and continuous monitoring for new tech/hazards, yielding moderate elasticity. Because disruption remains at or below 6, AI mainly augments peripheral tasks without reshaping the occupation's core, fitting the resilient category.

title: Occupational therapists
rationale: Core OT work centers on in-person observation of functional tasks, hands-on demonstration of exercises and adaptive techniques, home/workplace evaluations, and real-time interpersonal coaching of clients with physical or cognitive impairments—tasks that require physical presence and cannot be automated. AI can assist peripheral elements such as medical-history review, treatment-plan drafting, progress documentation, and equipment recommendations, producing only moderate disruption. Demand elasticity is moderate because an aging population and currently unmet needs (waitlists for pediatric and geriatric care, underserved regions) create room for expanded utilization if productivity rises, yet growth remains bounded by medical necessity, insurance rules, and the irreducible need for licensed human therapists. With disruption well below the high threshold, the occupation remains resilient overall.

title: Occupational therapy assistants and aides
rationale: Core tasks center on hands-on physical guidance of clients through exercises, adaptive daily-living skills, equipment use, and real-time interpersonal support that require physical presence, strength, and adaptability; AI can only assist peripheral documentation, scheduling, and progress tracking. Demand is driven primarily by medical necessity and an aging population rather than price, so even large productivity gains would expand access only modestly within insurance, regulatory, and clinical constraints. Because disruption remains low, the occupation stays resilient with AI touching the edges rather than reshaping the work.

title: Oil and gas workers
rationale: Core tasks are almost entirely physical and on-site—assembling, operating, repairing heavy drilling equipment, working at heights or in confined spaces, and handling materials in remote outdoor environments—so AI has limited reach beyond peripheral monitoring, predictive maintenance alerts, or automated drilling parameter optimization. Demand for oil and gas extraction is driven by energy markets, geology, and capital costs rather than labor productivity; cheaper/faster worker output mainly allows more barrels per rig or fewer crews, with only modest expansion of total wells given relatively inelastic oil demand and climate constraints. Because disruption remains low, the occupation is resilient: AI and automation trim some headcount growth but do not reshape the hands-on nature of the work.

title: Operations research analysts
rationale: Core work is almost entirely digital and cognitive—data collection/organization, quantitative modeling, forecasting, optimization, coding analytical tools, and writing recommendation reports—all of which sit squarely in AI’s current and near-term capabilities, driving a very high disruption score. Demand elasticity is high because sophisticated operations-research analysis remains cost-constrained for many mid-size and smaller organizations; 10x cheaper/faster modeling unlocks latent demand for continuous optimization of logistics, pricing, resource allocation, and supply chains across far more firms and use cases. The combination produces an augment outcome: each analyst becomes dramatically more productive while total volume of analysis expands enough to keep headcount stable or growing.

title: Opticians
rationale: Core tasks center on physical measurements of faces/eyes, hands-on frame fitting and adjustments requiring dexterity, contact-lens training, and in-person customer interaction; AI can assist peripheral elements such as frame recommendations, virtual try-ons, work-order generation, and inventory but leaves the presence-dependent fitting work largely intact. Demand for dispensing services is primarily driven by fixed vision-correction needs and demographic aging rather than price/speed; cheaper or faster service may modestly increase multi-pair purchases or updates but is constrained by the number of people needing eyewear and by online alternatives already capturing volume. Because disruption remains moderate, the occupation is resilient—AI reshapes sales and admin edges without transforming the core role.

title: Optometrists
rationale: AI already assists with retinal image analysis, disease screening (e.g., diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma), and interpretation of vision-test data, and will further automate diagnostic portions, but core daily work remains physical patient exams with specialized equipment, minor procedures, prescribing, and in-person counseling that require presence and clinical judgment. Demand for eye care is primarily demographic (aging population, rising myopia and diabetes) rather than heavily cost-suppressed, so 10x productivity gains would expand access modestly in underserved segments but not unlock large latent volume of additional exams or treatments. Because disruption stays moderate, the occupation is resilient: AI reshapes tools and throughput at the margin without displacing the human-centered core.

title: Orthotists and prosthetists
rationale: Core tasks center on in-person patient evaluation, physical measurement/fitting, hands-on device adjustment, and instruction, which require real-world presence, dexterity, and interpersonal skills; AI already assists design optimization, 3D scanning/CAD, material selection, and documentation but leaves the physical and clinical core intact, placing disruption firmly in the moderate mixed range. Demand is driven by aging, diabetes, obesity, and trauma, with meaningful latent expansion possible if devices become cheaper and more customized, unlocking better access and upgrades for underserved patients, yet overall volume remains constrained by medical need rather than unlimited. Because disruption stays at or below 6, AI reshapes peripheral knowledge work without transforming the occupation’s essential human-presence requirements, yielding a resilient net effect.

title: Painters, construction and maintenance
rationale: Core tasks—surface prep, scaffolding, brushing/rolling/spraying paint on irregular real-world structures—are almost entirely physical, on-site, and require human presence at heights or in confined spaces; AI assists only peripheral estimating or color visualization and remains far from automating the work. Demand for painting is only modestly elastic: cheaper/faster service could reduce DIY and encourage slightly more frequent redecoration or commercial work, but total volume is still constrained by the stock of buildings, maintenance cycles, and new construction rates. With disruption well below the threshold that reshapes the occupation, the net effect is resilient regardless of modest elasticity.

title: Painting and coating workers
rationale: Core tasks center on physical surface preparation, manual or machine-assisted coating application, thickness measurement, and equipment maintenance in factory or repair settings, with only peripheral digital elements like machine programming or gauge monitoring; AI can aid quality inspection via vision systems or color matching but leaves the hands-on, presence-required work largely unchanged. Demand for painting and coating is tightly coupled to fixed volumes of manufactured goods and vehicle repairs rather than being cost-suppressed, so productivity gains primarily reduce headcount instead of unlocking large new volumes of output. The low disruption score therefore places the occupation in the resilient category regardless of modest elasticity.

title: Paralegals and legal assistants
rationale: Core tasks—legal research, document drafting, fact gathering, organizing case files, and preparing correspondence—are almost entirely digital/cognitive and already being materially automated by tools like CoCounsel and Harvey AI, placing the occupation squarely in the 8-9 band. Demand elasticity is low because total legal caseloads and court capacity are structurally constrained; while cheaper support work may unlock some latent access-to-justice demand, it will not expand nearly enough to offset 10x productivity gains, so headcount contracts. This matches the replace category (disruption ≥7 and elasticity ≤4), consistent with BLS’s own projection of zero growth driven by AI efficiency.

title: Personal financial advisors
rationale: Core tasks such as investment research, portfolio construction, risk assessment, monitoring, and generating recommendations are predominantly cognitive and digital, already materially assisted by robo-advisors and generative AI tools, even as client meetings, trust-building, and sales remain human-centric. Demand is highly elastic because high fees currently suppress usage among middle-income households and younger savers; dramatically cheaper AI-augmented advice unlocks large latent markets for retirement, education, and tax planning, especially amid aging demographics and the shift from pensions. Productivity gains therefore expand total service volume rather than purely contracting headcount, allowing advisors who adopt AI to serve far more clients. This produces the classic augment pattern of stable-to-growing employment with substantially higher output per worker.

title: Pest control workers
rationale: Core tasks center on physical on-site inspection of crawl spaces and structures, applying pesticides, setting traps, and creating barriers in unpredictable real-world environments, so AI only assists peripheral elements like pest photo identification, treatment recommendations, cost estimation, scheduling, and bookkeeping. Demand has moderate elasticity because lower costs and faster service could shift more households and businesses from DIY to professional or preventive contracts and expand commercial work, yet total volume remains bounded by the stock of buildings and actual infestation rates rather than expanding without limit. With disruption well below the high threshold, the occupation stays resilient as AI does not reshape the hands-on core work.

title: Petroleum engineers
rationale: Core tasks center on reservoir data analysis, extraction design, drilling plans, production optimization, and recovery modeling—predominantly cognitive/digital work where AI tools already deliver material gains in simulation, seismic interpretation, and predictive analytics, with a clear trajectory toward deeper automation even if occasional site oversight remains. Demand elasticity is low because oil/gas volumes are set by commodity prices, geology, capital intensity, and regulation rather than engineering cost or speed; cheaper/faster engineering unlocks only modest extra recovery or adjacent work in CCS/geothermal. High disruption paired with limited demand expansion therefore implies AI absorbs substantial core work and headcount contracts.

title: Pharmacists
rationale: Core pharmacist work is predominantly cognitive and language-based—verifying prescriptions, screening interactions/allergies, dosing, therapy recommendations, and patient/physician counseling—which AI already assists via decision-support systems and will further automate or accelerate substantially over the next decade; physical elements (vaccinations, limited compounding, in-person presence) and legal accountability prevent full replacement. Demand elasticity is moderate because prescription volume itself is relatively fixed by physician orders and population health needs, yet cheaper/faster pharmacist capacity unlocks meaningful expansion in under-provided clinical services such as medication therapy management, chronic-care counseling, and team-based hospital roles. The combination produces restructuring: routine dispensing and verification shrink while higher-value clinical and advisory work grows, requiring skill shifts toward AI oversight, complex cases, and direct patient care.

title: Pharmacy technicians
rationale: Pharmacy technicians combine physical tasks (measuring, packaging, labeling, inventory handling, and customer-facing work) that require on-site presence with digital/admin work (data entry, insurance claims, phone triage) that AI and existing automated dispensing systems already assist, producing moderate disruption overall. Demand is driven mainly by fixed demographic and clinical factors—aging populations and chronic disease prescriptions—rather than the labor cost of technicians, so large productivity gains unlock only limited extra volume under regulatory and medical constraints. Because disruption stays in the moderate range, the occupation remains resilient: AI will streamline peripheral and routine elements while core human presence and oversight persist.

title: Phlebotomists
rationale: Core duties center on physical blood draws requiring dexterity, patient calming, vein access under variable conditions, and sterile technique—tasks that remain almost entirely hands-on and presence-dependent; AI currently aids only peripheral steps such as identity verification, labeling, and database entry, with robotic or AI-guided systems still far from routine clinical use. Demand for draws is driven by physician orders, demographics, and medical necessity rather than price or speed, so even large productivity gains unlock only modest additional volume (e.g., slightly more screening or home collections) rather than explosive expansion. Because disruption stays low, the occupation is resilient: AI touches administration but leaves the essential work and headcount trajectory largely intact.

title: Photographers
rationale: Core tasks mix physical on-location capture, client interaction, lighting/equipment handling, and real-world presence (weddings, portraits, news, commercial shoots) with digital post-processing and planning; AI already materially assists editing, enhancement, and composition suggestions but cannot replace the unpredictable real-world shooting that defines most work, keeping disruption moderate. Cheaper/faster output via AI tools would unlock meaningful latent demand in e-commerce product imagery, marketing content, and affordable personal/event photography, though event volume and smartphone/stock alternatives limit full expansion. Because disruption remains moderate, AI primarily augments tools and workflows without reshaping the occupation's physical-creative core, fitting the resilient category.

title: Physical therapist assistants and aides
rationale: Core tasks center on hands-on patient interaction—guiding exercises, massage, stretching, gait training, lifting/moving patients, and equipment setup—which require physical presence, dexterity, and stamina that AI cannot replace in the next decade; AI only peripherally aids documentation, scheduling, or progress notes. Demand elasticity is moderate because lower costs would expand access for aging populations, chronic conditions, and underserved patients, unlocking more sessions and home-care utilization, yet insurance rules, patient physical limits, and finite clinical need cap unlimited growth. With disruption well below the high threshold, the occupation remains resilient as AI touches only admin edges while human physical care stays essential.

title: Physical therapists
rationale: Core PT work centers on real-time physical observation of movement, hands-on manual therapy, patient handling, and in-person exercise demonstration, all of which require human presence and dexterity; AI already assists secondary tasks such as chart review, gait analysis from video, plan drafting, and documentation but does not displace the physical core, placing disruption firmly in the moderate mixed range. Demand is currently constrained by cost, insurance session limits, and access shortages, so large productivity or price improvements would unlock substantially more utilization for aging populations, chronic conditions, preventive wellness, and underserved patients. Because disruption remains only moderate, the occupation is resilient: AI augments peripheral cognitive work while the hands-on service model and expanding need keep headcount stable or growing.

title: Physician assistants
rationale: Core PA work mixes cognitive tasks (history review, diagnosis, test interpretation, prescribing, patient education) that AI already assists via diagnostic tools, ambient documentation, and decision support with irreplaceable physical presence for exams, procedures like suturing or casting, and real-time patient interaction under variable clinical conditions, placing it firmly in the moderate range. Demand elasticity is high because healthcare access remains constrained by cost, wait times, and provider shortages—especially primary care, rural, and chronic-disease management—so large productivity gains would unlock substantially more visits and services rather than simply shrinking headcount. With disruption only moderate, AI reshapes peripheral workflows and augments decision-making without displacing the occupation’s essential human-in-the-loop role, yielding a resilient net effect consistent with BLS’s already strong projected growth.

title: Physicians and surgeons
rationale: Core physician and surgeon work mixes cognitive tasks (diagnosis, test interpretation, treatment planning, documentation) that AI already assists via imaging tools, ambient scribes, and decision support with irreplaceable physical and presence-based tasks (exams, procedures, surgery, real-time patient counseling and crisis management), keeping disruption moderate. Demand elasticity is high because cost, wait times, and access barriers currently suppress large volumes of care; 10x productivity gains would unlock more preventive visits, chronic-disease management, elective procedures, mental-health services, and care in underserved markets. With disruption remaining at or below the moderate threshold, AI primarily augments peripheral and knowledge components without reshaping the occupation’s human-centered core, producing a resilient net effect.

title: Physicists and astronomers
rationale: Core tasks such as theory and model development, mathematical analysis of data, software coding for simulations, equipment design via computation, proposal writing, and paper drafting are almost entirely cognitive and digital, placing them squarely in AI’s path; current tools already accelerate literature synthesis, hypothesis generation, and numerical work, with experimental and observational components increasingly AI-assisted even if physical apparatus remains. Demand is highly elastic because fundamental and applied physics research is bottlenecked by researcher time and cost; 10x productivity would unlock far more industrial R&D, materials discovery, quantum and fusion projects, medical-physics applications, and space science that are currently suppressed by limited grants and slow cycles. Consequently headcount is expected to hold or grow as total scientific output expands, fitting the augment category.

title: Plumbers, pipefitters, and steamfitters
rationale: Core tasks center on physical installation, repair, welding, and troubleshooting of pipes and fixtures in unpredictable real-world sites, requiring strength, dexterity, and on-site presence that AI cannot perform; AI only assists peripheral elements like cost estimates, BIM blueprint analysis, and code checks. Demand is only modestly elastic because plumbing needs are largely fixed by building stock, maintenance cycles, and construction volume rather than being heavily cost-suppressed, so cheaper/faster work unlocks limited extra renovations or upgrades but not massive new consumption. With disruption well below the high threshold, the occupation remains resilient as AI does not reshape the hands-on core work.

title: Podiatrists
rationale: Podiatrists' core duties center on physical exams, hands-on nonsurgical treatments, and foot/ankle surgery that require real-world presence and manual skill; AI can assist with x-ray interpretation, diagnostic suggestions, charting, and research but leaves the majority of daily work largely unchanged, producing only moderate disruption. Demand is driven by medical necessity (diabetes, aging, injuries) rather than latent unmet desire for more procedures, so even large productivity gains would expand volume only modestly under regulatory and clinical constraints. With disruption at a moderate level, the occupation remains resilient: AI tools will improve efficiency at the margins without displacing or fundamentally restructuring the role.

title: Police and detectives
rationale: Core duties such as patrolling, responding to calls, making arrests, securing crime scenes, and physical intervention require real-world presence, physical capability, and on-the-spot judgment that AI cannot replace, though AI already assists peripheral tasks like report writing, database searches, evidence analysis, and predictive tools. Demand is constrained by government budgets, political decisions, crime incidence rates, and social limits on policing intensity, so productivity gains are unlikely to unlock large latent expansion in headcount. Because disruption remains moderate, the occupation is resilient: AI reshapes support functions without displacing the human-centered core of the work.

title: Political scientists
rationale: Core tasks—researching political systems, collecting and analyzing survey/historical/voter data, developing theories, evaluating policies, forecasting trends, and writing/publishing reports—are almost entirely cognitive, language-based, and digital, already materially assisted by LLMs for synthesis, modeling, and drafting, with rapid further trajectory. Demand is heavily constrained by federal budgets (67% of jobs), institutional funding, and limited positions in think tanks or consulting, so productivity gains do not unlock dramatic new consumption of political analysis the way cheaper software or content does. High disruption combined with low elasticity therefore implies AI absorbs substantial core work without offsetting headcount growth, producing contraction.

title: Postal service workers
rationale: Core tasks for the majority of workers (mail carriers) remain physical—walking/driving routes, lifting parcels, and outdoor delivery in variable conditions—while AI mainly optimizes routing, enhances OCR/sorting machinery, and supports kiosks or chat for clerks; this is mixed assistance rather than replacement of hands-on work. Demand is inelastic because letter volume is already structurally declining due to digital substitution and package growth is constrained by competition and fixed logistics needs, so productivity gains simply enlarge routes or cut headcount rather than expand total mail volume. The occupation therefore fits resilient: AI touches peripherals and accelerates existing automation trends but does not reshape the physical core, consistent with BLS’s projected mild decline.

title: Postsecondary education administrators
rationale: Core tasks such as application review and data analysis, student-record maintenance, course scheduling, budget management, and policy drafting are predominantly cognitive, language-based, and digital; AI tools already perform screening, analytics, optimization, and document generation, materially reshaping daily work even while interpersonal advising and faculty relations remain human. Demand is structurally capped by the fixed number of institutions, slow demographic enrollment trends, and state/institutional budgets, so 10x productivity gains will not unlock large latent consumption of administrative services. Productivity improvements therefore translate mainly into fewer administrators per campus rather than expanded headcount. High disruption combined with low elasticity places the occupation in the replace category.

title: Postsecondary teachers
rationale: Core tasks such as syllabus and lesson design, content creation, grading, literature review, data analysis, and scholarly writing are predominantly cognitive and language-based, already materially assisted by AI tools today and on a clear trajectory for deeper automation, while live teaching, mentoring, and original research still require human judgment and presence. Demand for postsecondary instruction and research is highly elastic because high tuition and limited access currently suppress enrollment, lifelong learning, and research output; dramatically cheaper and more scalable delivery unlocks larger student volumes, more personalized and continuous education, and expanded knowledge production. High disruption combined with high elasticity means productivity gains are absorbed by greater total output rather than headcount contraction, so the occupation is augmented.

title: Power plant operators, distributors, and dispatchers
rationale: Core tasks center on control-room monitoring of meters/gauges, adjusting flows, and responding to plant conditions, which are mixed digital-cognitive work that AI already assists via smart-grid analytics, predictive maintenance, and anomaly detection, yet still require on-site human presence for physical rounds, mechanical interventions, and safety-critical decisions (especially nuclear licensing). This yields moderate disruption rather than full automation of the role. Elasticity is low because operator headcount is driven by the fixed number and capacity of generating assets plus regulatory staffing minima, not by latent demand; electricity consumption may grow but does not scale operator needs proportionally when productivity rises, as BLS already projects net declines from efficiency gains. The combination keeps the occupation resilient: AI reshapes peripheral monitoring but leaves the core human-in-the-loop plant control intact.

title: Preschool and childcare center directors
rationale: Core duties center on on-site staff supervision, parent meetings, classroom visits, facility compliance, and interpersonal leadership with young children, which require physical presence and human judgment that AI cannot replace, though AI already assists peripheral knowledge tasks such as budgeting, curriculum drafting, policy writing, and parent communications, producing only moderate disruption. Demand elasticity is low because the number of centers is structurally capped by birth rates, child-staff ratios, licensing rules, and physical facilities; even if AI lowers administrative costs, latent demand expansion is limited and unlikely to absorb large productivity gains. The combination keeps the occupation resilient: AI touches admin edges without reshaping the essential human-centered management role.

title: Preschool teachers
rationale: Core preschool work is overwhelmingly physical and presence-based—real-time play facilitation, emotional regulation, safety supervision, and hands-on skill-building with unpredictable toddlers—which AI cannot perform; tools only assist peripheral tasks like lesson ideation, progress notes, and parent messaging. Demand has moderate elasticity because high childcare costs currently suppress access, so cheaper/more efficient services could modestly expand enrollment and hours, yet growth remains capped by fixed child demographics and strict regulatory ratios. With disruption well below the high threshold, the occupation stays resilient: AI touches the edges without reshaping daily classroom reality or headcount drivers.

title: Private detectives and investigators
rationale: Core duties mix digital research, record analysis, and report writing (already AI-assisted via OSINT tools, data scraping, and generation) with irreplaceable physical tasks like in-person interviews, undercover observation, and real-world surveillance that require presence, judgment under uncertainty, and legal compliance. This yields moderate disruption similar to police or nursing roles. Elasticity is moderate because cheaper/faster investigations unlock some latent demand for background checks, fraud probes, and personal matters among businesses and individuals, yet regulatory limits, privacy laws, and case-specific nature of demand prevent explosive growth. Net effect is resilient as AI reshapes peripherals without displacing the occupation's human-centric core.

title: Probation officers and correctional treatment specialists
rationale: Core work centers on in-person interviews, home and workplace visits, court testimony, drug testing, and building relationships with high-risk clients in unpredictable settings, all of which require physical presence and human judgment that AI cannot replace; AI can meaningfully assist only peripheral tasks such as report drafting, risk scoring, and resource matching, producing moderate disruption. Demand is set by crime rates, sentencing policy, and fixed government corrections budgets rather than price or speed, so even large productivity gains would mainly raise caseloads or free limited funds rather than expand total headcount. Because disruption remains moderate, the occupation is resilient: AI touches administrative edges without reshaping the essential field and interpersonal work.

title: Producers and directors
rationale: Core tasks center on creative judgment, script selection, casting, budgeting, and postproduction oversight—predominantly cognitive and digital work where AI already assists with script analysis, generative storyboarding, VFX, editing, scheduling optimization, and promo materials, materially reshaping workflows even if human vision and on-set leadership remain essential. Demand is highly elastic because production cost and speed have long constrained output; dramatically cheaper/faster content creation unlocks far more films, streaming series, ads, and digital video across platforms with near-unlimited appetite for content. This combination means AI multiplies output per worker while expanding the overall market enough to support stable or growing headcount for those who adapt.

title: Project management specialists
rationale: Core work is predominantly cognitive and digital—plan development, risk/cost monitoring, document production, stakeholder communication, and milestone tracking—where AI tools already generate schedules, draft plans, summarize status, and surface risks, making disruption high even though interpersonal leadership and ambiguous problem-solving still require humans. Elasticity is moderate because cheaper, faster project coordination unlocks more formal management of smaller initiatives and IT/process projects, yet overall project volume remains constrained by capital, labor, and physical resources rather than expanding without bound. The combination produces restructure: the role persists but shifts heavily toward AI orchestration, strategic judgment, and client-facing skills, displacing those who do not adapt.

title: Property appraisers and assessors
rationale: Core work mixes physical site inspections and photography with heavy cognitive tasks—verifying records, analyzing comps, applying mass-appraisal models, and writing valuation reports—where AI and existing automated valuation models already deliver material productivity gains and will expand further via computer vision and generative reporting. Demand for appraisals and assessments is largely fixed by real-estate transaction volumes, mortgage regulations, and local tax rolls; these volumes do not expand dramatically when the service becomes cheaper or faster. High disruption combined with low elasticity therefore implies AI absorbs a large share of the work without offsetting growth in total output, producing net headcount contraction.

title: Property, real estate, and community association managers
rationale: Core duties mix physical on-site work (inspections, showing units, investigating complaints, contractor oversight) that requires human presence with knowledge/admin tasks (budgets, records, leasing, compliance) where AI already assists via property software, chatbots, predictive maintenance, and virtual tours, yielding moderate disruption. Demand is largely anchored to the fixed stock of residential/commercial properties and housing growth, with only partial expansion possible if lower costs induce more small owners to outsource management. Because disruption remains moderate, AI reshapes peripheral processes without transforming the occupation’s core, fitting the resilient category.

title: Psychiatric technicians and aides
rationale: Core duties center on physical presence, hands-on assistance with daily living, patient restraint, escorting, and real-time observation of unpredictable behavior in facilities—tasks that remain almost entirely non-digital and require human stamina, compassion, and interpersonal skills; AI can only touch peripheral documentation or sensor-based alerts. Demand for mental-health support has latent room to expand if costs fall, given under-treatment and projected patient growth, yet is constrained by public funding, facility capacity, and regulatory limits, producing only moderate elasticity. Because disruption stays low, the occupation remains resilient overall.

title: Psychologists
rationale: Core tasks such as interviewing, diagnosing disorders, analyzing behavioral patterns, research, and report-writing are predominantly cognitive and language-based, with AI already providing material assistance via clinical note scribes, assessment scoring, literature synthesis, and even preliminary chatbot triage; human empathy, rapport-building, and real-time observation remain essential but do not prevent high disruption of the knowledge-work core. Demand for psychological services is heavily suppressed by cost, wait times, and access barriers amid a well-documented mental-health shortage, so 10x productivity gains would unlock substantial latent demand from individuals, schools, workplaces, and underserved populations. High disruption combined with high elasticity therefore produces an augment outcome: each psychologist handles far more cases and research while total employment holds steady or grows as more services are consumed.

title: Public relations and fundraising managers
rationale: Core work is predominantly knowledge- and language-based—writing press releases, drafting speeches, audience analysis, campaign strategy, grant applications, and trend monitoring—where generative AI already materially accelerates content production, personalization, and data-driven targeting, even as face-to-face donor meetings, crisis judgment, and staff leadership remain human. Elasticity is high because cost and speed currently suppress sophisticated PR and fundraising for many smaller organizations and nonprofits; dramatically cheaper output unlocks far more campaigns, content volume, donor outreach, and reputation management across more entities. The combination produces an augment outcome: each manager handles far higher volume while total demand for image and fundraising services expands enough to keep headcount stable or growing.

title: Public relations specialists
rationale: Core tasks such as writing press releases, drafting speeches, creating social media content, and evaluating public opinion via digital channels are almost entirely language-based and cognitive, placing them squarely in the path of generative AI that already drafts, analyzes sentiment, and iterates messaging at high quality. Elasticity is moderate because dramatically cheaper and faster PR unlocks meaningful new demand from small businesses, nonprofits, personal brands, and higher-volume campaigns that were previously cost-prohibitive, yet total organizational need for reputation management remains bounded by attention limits and strategic priorities rather than expanding without bound. High disruption combined with only moderate demand expansion means the occupation survives but restructures: pure content production shrinks while roles emphasizing strategy, media relationships, crisis judgment, and AI oversight expand, displacing those who fail to adapt.

title: Public safety telecommunicators
rationale: Core tasks are almost entirely language-based, cognitive, and digital—real-time call handling, triage per protocols, instruction-giving, multi-unit coordination, and logging—which AI already assists via speech-to-text, NLP triage, translation, CAD suggestions, and automated logging, with rapid trajectory toward handling routine and many complex interactions. Demand for the service is driven by exogenous emergency volume and population, not price or speed, so 10x productivity gains produce little expansion beyond marginal coverage improvements and are constrained by public budgets and fixed incident rates. This combination of high disruption and low elasticity means AI absorbs substantial core work without offsetting demand growth, producing net headcount contraction.

title: Purchasing managers, buyers, and purchasing agents
rationale: Core tasks such as analyzing price proposals and financial reports, evaluating suppliers on data, monitoring contracts, and maintaining inventory/cost records are predominantly cognitive and digital, with AI tools already automating spend analysis, risk scoring, and proposal review; plant visits, trade shows, and live negotiation remain human-centric but are a minority of daily work, placing disruption firmly in the high range. Demand elasticity is moderate because the volume of goods and services organizations must procure is largely fixed by business activity rather than procurement cost, yet cheaper AI-augmented analysis can expand sophisticated sourcing for SMEs and enable more frequent supplier re-evaluation. High disruption combined with only moderate demand expansion means the occupation persists but requires substantial skill shifts toward AI oversight, strategic relationship management, and complex judgment, fitting restructure.

title: Quality control inspectors
rationale: AI computer vision, 3D scanners, CMMs, and automated sensor systems already perform core defect detection, measurement, and data analysis tasks that once required human inspectors, with rapid trajectory toward fuller automation of testing and process monitoring even as residual physical handling persists. Demand for quality inspection is tightly coupled to manufacturing volumes rather than heavily suppressed by inspection cost, so 10x cheaper/faster AI-driven QC mainly enables fuller sampling or continuous monitoring without unlocking dramatically higher total output of the service. High disruption combined with low elasticity means AI absorbs the bulk of the work and headcount contracts rather than expanding.

title: Radiation therapists
rationale: Core duties center on physical patient positioning, real-time machine operation of linear accelerators, safety monitoring, and in-person interaction during treatment sessions, so AI can assist with imaging analysis, planning support, calibration checks, and records but cannot remove the need for human presence and hands-on clinical work. Demand is driven almost entirely by cancer incidence and prescribed treatment courses rather than price or speed; lower costs or higher productivity do not generate large volumes of additional therapy sessions, and efficiency gains already constrain employment growth. Because disruption remains only moderate, the occupation falls into the resilient category regardless of the low elasticity.

title: Radiologic and MRI technologists
rationale: Core tasks center on physical patient positioning, equipment operation, radiation/MRI safety shielding, and real-time interpersonal care for stressed or injured patients, all of which require on-site human presence; AI can assist with protocol selection, image quality checks, and records but leaves the hands-on workflow largely intact, producing only moderate disruption. Demand for imaging exams is driven by physician orders, clinical necessity, aging demographics, and insurance rules rather than price or speed, so even large productivity gains would not unlock dramatically higher volumes of scans. Because disruption remains in the moderate range, the occupation is resilient: AI tools will improve efficiency at the margins without reshaping the fundamental role or headcount trajectory.

title: Railroad workers
rationale: Core tasks center on physical presence—operating locomotives, observing tracks, coupling cars, yard switching, and real-time safety coordination—which AI cannot fully replace; current tools mainly assist peripheral functions like predictive maintenance, signal optimization, and scheduling. Demand for rail freight and passenger service is constrained by infrastructure capacity, economic activity, and modal competition rather than labor cost, so productivity gains from automation primarily reduce headcount rather than expand total volume. With disruption only moderate, the occupation remains resilient overall even as efficiency improvements continue to limit employment growth.

title: Real estate brokers and sales agents
rationale: AI already materially assists core knowledge tasks such as comparative market analysis, pricing advice, listing generation, digital marketing, and document preparation, and will deepen this over the next decade, but physical property showings, open houses, local networking, and high-stakes interpersonal negotiations still require human presence and trust. Demand for brokerage services is structurally capped by the volume of real estate transactions, which is driven by interest rates, inventory, demographics, and life events rather than agent cost or speed; cheaper/faster service unlocks only limited additional volume. Because disruption remains at the high end of moderate rather than fully transforming the occupation, the net effect is resilient.

title: Receptionists
rationale: Core receptionist duties—answering phones, scheduling, data entry, correspondence, and information provision—are predominantly language-based, digital, and cognitive, already being displaced by AI voice agents, chatbots, online booking systems, and virtual reception tools, even as limited physical greeting and security roles persist in settings like healthcare. This yields high disruption given current AI utility and rapid trajectory. Elasticity is low because reception demand is largely fixed by the number of offices, clinics, and facilities rather than suppressed by cost; cheaper/faster service does not unlock dramatically more visitor handling or call volume. High disruption combined with low elasticity therefore maps to replace, with AI absorbing tasks and producing net headcount contraction.

title: Recreation workers
rationale: Core duties center on in-person group leadership, real-time instruction, safety oversight, first aid, equipment handling, and interpersonal motivation across outdoor/indoor settings—tasks that are physical, adaptive, and presence-dependent, so AI only touches peripheral admin such as calendars, newsletters, or activity-idea generation. Demand shows moderate elasticity because lower organization costs could expand program offerings in parks, senior facilities, and community centers amid rising wellness interest, yet growth remains constrained by physical facilities, participant free time, and public budgets. With disruption well below the high threshold, the occupation stays resilient as AI does not reshape the hands-on core.

title: Recreational therapists
