rationale: Core work centers on in-person patient engagement through sports, games, community outings, arts, and adaptive activities that require physical presence, real-time motivation, empathy, and hands-on assistance—tasks AI cannot perform—while AI only assists peripheral elements like record review, plan drafting, and progress documentation. Demand is constrained by clinical need, insurance reimbursement, facility funding, and regulatory structures rather than pure price or speed, so even large productivity gains would unlock only limited additional volume among aging or mental-health populations. Because disruption remains moderate, the occupation is resilient: AI touches planning and admin but leaves the essential therapeutic interaction intact.

title: Registered nurses
rationale: Core RN duties center on physical patient assessment, medication administration, equipment operation, hands-on monitoring, and in-person emotional support that require unpredictable real-world presence, so AI mainly assists peripheral knowledge tasks such as charting, data analysis, and care-plan suggestions rather than replacing the occupation’s essence. Demand elasticity is moderate because an aging population and rising chronic conditions already drive growth, and cheaper/faster nursing productivity would unlock more home care, preventive education, and access in underserved settings without fully saturating need. The combination keeps the occupation in the resilient category: AI changes workflows at the margins but does not fundamentally reshape or eliminate the need for human nurses.

title: Rehabilitation counselors
rationale: Core duties center on interpersonal counseling, empathy-driven relationship building, in-person client evaluation, employer advocacy, and navigating complex real-world disability accommodations—tasks that require human presence and soft skills AI can only peripherally assist via documentation, resource search, or plan drafting. Demand elasticity is moderate because cheaper/faster service delivery would expand access for aging populations, veterans, and underserved clients currently limited by budgets, allowing more comprehensive support without fully offsetting productivity gains. Net effect is resilient as AI remains assistive rather than transformative to the occupation's relational core.

title: Respiratory therapists
rationale: Core duties center on hands-on patient examination, physical treatments such as chest physiotherapy, ventilator setup/monitoring in acute settings, and real-time clinical presence, so AI can only assist peripheral knowledge tasks like interpreting pulmonary function data, suggesting plans, or automating records. Demand is driven primarily by fixed demographic and disease prevalence factors (aging population, COPD, emergencies) with only moderate expansion possible via cheaper home care or outpatient access; productivity gains will not unlock unlimited new volume. Because disruption remains moderate, the occupation is resilient—AI augments efficiency at the edges without reshaping the essential human-delivered clinical work.

title: Retail sales workers
rationale: Core tasks mix physical presence (greeting, demonstrating products, stocking, handling merchandise and security) with language/cognitive elements (recommendations, explanations, answering questions, promotions), so AI tools already assist via POS systems, inventory software, and recommendation engines but cannot eliminate the need for in-store human interaction and unpredictable real-world presence. Elasticity is low because demand for physical retail assistance is constrained by store foot traffic, e-commerce substitution, and fixed consumer shopping patterns; productivity gains (self-checkout, AI kiosks) historically shrink headcount rather than unlock large latent demand for more sales help. With disruption only moderate, the occupation remains resilient overall even as tools change peripheral workflows.

title: Roofers
rationale: Core roofing tasks—climbing, lifting heavy materials, cutting and fastening shingles or membranes, working at heights outdoors—are almost entirely physical and site-specific, placing the occupation at the minimal end of the disruption scale; AI can at best assist with peripheral estimating, drone inspection, or material calculation. Demand is largely tied to the existing building stock, weather damage, and new construction volume rather than being heavily suppressed by price, so even large productivity gains would produce only modest expansion in total roofing work. Because disruption remains far below the threshold that reshapes daily tasks, the occupation is resilient: AI stays on the periphery and headcount continues to track construction and repair needs.

title: Sales engineers
rationale: Core tasks such as preparing technical presentations, analyzing customer requirements, customizing recommendations, and generating support materials are predominantly knowledge- and language-based work where current AI tools already materially accelerate content creation, personalization, and data synthesis, though relationship-building, live persuasion, and negotiation still require human presence. If AI made the role 10x faster and cheaper, lower sales-process costs would unlock additional mid-market and complex-product deals that were previously uneconomical, producing meaningful but not unlimited demand expansion constrained by overall market size and sales-cycle realities. This combination of high disruption with moderate elasticity means the occupation persists but shifts substantially toward AI-fluent high-touch selling; workers who fail to adapt face displacement while those who master the new tools thrive.

title: Sales managers
rationale: Sales managers' core work is predominantly knowledge-based—data analysis, forecasting, goal-setting, budgeting, strategy development, and training design—all of which AI tools already materially accelerate via CRM analytics, generative planning, and automated reporting, even while people-leadership and escalated interpersonal resolution remain human. Demand elasticity is only moderate because cheaper, faster sales management unlocks some expansion (more sophisticated strategies, broader market coverage, better support for growing sales forces) but is constrained by organizational structure, span-of-control norms, and the finite number of sales organizations; productivity gains therefore shift skill requirements more than they expand headcount. This combination of high disruption with moderate elasticity produces a restructured occupation in which adaptive managers thrive with AI leverage while others are displaced.

title: School and career counselors and advisors
rationale: Core tasks center on interpersonal counseling, empathy-driven advising for social/behavioral issues, crisis response, and in-person collaboration with students, families, and staff—work that requires unpredictable human presence and trust—while AI only assists peripheral elements like data analysis of attendance/performance, aptitude matching, college/career information delivery, resume drafting, and record-keeping. This yields moderate disruption as AI tools already help knowledge portions but leave the relational core intact over the next decade. Elasticity is moderate because high student-to-counselor ratios and limited access to career coaching create some latent demand that cheaper/faster services could unlock (especially private career advising and expanded school programs), yet K-12 and higher-ed funding formulas, credentialing rules, and fixed student populations constrain dramatic expansion. With disruption at or below 6, the occupation remains resilient as AI augments edges without reshaping daily human-centered work.

title: Secretaries and administrative assistants
rationale: Core tasks—document drafting and editing, scheduling, email/phone handling, database maintenance, basic bookkeeping, and report preparation—are almost entirely digital, cognitive, and language-based, already being materially automated by generative AI, scheduling agents, and office software; physical or unpredictable real-world elements are peripheral. Demand for administrative support is largely a fixed cost of organizational activity rather than a service with large latent unmet need, so 10x productivity gains primarily allow managers and staff to self-serve or consolidate roles rather than expand total headcount. This combination of very high disruption and low elasticity produces net replacement pressure, consistent with BLS projections of flat-to-declining employment driven by technology.

title: Securities, commodities, and financial services sales agents
rationale: Core tasks center on market monitoring, financial analysis, trade execution, advice generation, and client pitches—all predominantly digital/cognitive work where AI already delivers material value via algorithmic trading, robo-advisors, automated research, and personalized outreach tools, with further trajectory toward handling routine recommendations and initial client screening. Elasticity is moderate because cheaper/faster advice and underwriting can expand access for retail investors and smaller firms currently priced out, yet overall deal volume and securities demand remain constrained by macroeconomic activity, regulation, and trust requirements rather than pure cost. This produces a restructure outcome: high disruption forces a shift toward AI-augmented relationship management and complex advisory skills, while moderate demand growth absorbs only part of the productivity gains, displacing those who fail to adapt.

title: Security guards and gambling surveillance officers
rationale: Core tasks center on physical presence, patrolling, access control, emergency response, and real-time deterrence, which require human judgment and on-site action that AI cannot fully automate; AI already assists video monitoring, anomaly detection, and report writing, producing a mixed profile similar to police officers. Demand for security services is driven more by crime risk, regulations, and asset values than by price, so even large productivity gains unlock only limited additional coverage rather than dramatic expansion. Because disruption remains moderate, AI reshapes peripheral monitoring duties without displacing the occupation’s essential human-presence core, fitting the resilient category.

title: Semiconductor processing technicians
rationale: Core tasks center on physical cleanroom presence—loading wafers, operating/adjusting specialized equipment, performing hands-on inspections with microscopes, and intervening for repairs or quality issues—while AI already aids peripheral monitoring, process data analysis, and yield optimization; this mixed profile yields moderate disruption. Elasticity is high because semiconductor demand is exploding (AI chips, electronics, CHIPS Act capacity expansion) and is not fixed, so productivity gains expand total output and fab activity rather than purely shrinking headcount. Net effect is therefore resilient: AI touches knowledge and control layers but leaves the essential on-site manufacturing role intact.

title: Set and exhibit designers
rationale: Core work is predominantly cognitive and digital—script analysis, conceptual design, CAD/3D modeling, budgeting, and visualization—where generative AI already produces concept art, layout variants, and renderings at high speed, though physical installation oversight, on-site collaboration, and real-world constructability still require human presence. Demand elasticity is moderate because lower design costs can unlock more indie productions, temporary exhibits, trade-show builds, and frequent museum rotations, yet overall volume remains constrained by venue capacity, construction budgets, and arts funding. High disruption therefore forces a substantial skill shift toward AI orchestration and creative direction while moderate demand growth prevents pure headcount collapse, producing a restructured occupation rather than outright replacement or pure augmentation.

title: Sheet metal workers
rationale: Core tasks center on physical fabrication, measuring, cutting, welding, maneuvering heavy sheets, and on-site installation of ducts/roofs/gutters, which demand strength, dexterity, and real-world presence in variable construction environments; AI and automation already aid CADD design, CNC cutting, and shop machinery but remain peripheral to the hands-on work. Demand is largely tied to building construction volumes and HVAC retrofits, so productivity gains (cheaper ducts or faster installs) unlock only modest extra activity such as energy-efficiency upgrades rather than order-of-magnitude expansion. Because disruption stays low-to-moderate, the occupation is resilient: AI touches planning and shop automation without reshaping the essential physical role.

title: Skincare specialists
rationale: Core duties—facials, massages, waxing/laser hair removal, product application, and in-person skin evaluation—are overwhelmingly physical and require real-world client presence, so AI only touches peripheral tasks such as photo-based skin analysis apps, product recommendations, scheduling, and client education. Demand elasticity is moderate because lower prices and faster service could modestly expand frequency of visits and reach new clients (men, younger consumers, mini-sessions), yet time constraints, personal preference, and the experiential nature of treatments prevent unlimited growth. With disruption well below the high threshold, the occupation remains resilient: AI augments advice and admin without reshaping the hands-on work that defines the role.

title: Small engine mechanics
rationale: Core work is overwhelmingly physical and manual—disassembling engines, replacing parts with hand tools, onsite or shop-floor repairs requiring dexterity and real-world presence—so AI only touches peripheral diagnostics, records, and customer communication. Demand for repairs is largely fixed by the existing stock of motorcycles, boats, and outdoor equipment plus seasonal usage patterns; cheaper or faster service unlocks only modest extra maintenance rather than large new volume. Because disruption stays low, the occupation remains resilient regardless of modest elasticity.

title: Social and community service managers
rationale: Core tasks such as data analysis for program effectiveness, writing funding proposals, administrative oversight, budgeting, and planning outreach are predominantly knowledge- and language-based work where current AI tools already provide material assistance and will deepen further. Human elements like stakeholder engagement, staff supervision of frontline social workers, community presence, and fundraising relationships prevent full automation but still leave the role highly exposed. Demand elasticity is moderate because cheaper, faster management can unlock more programs to address latent needs among aging populations and substance-abuse treatment, yet public budgets, grant cycles, and regulatory structures cap unlimited expansion. The result is a restructured occupation in which AI-fluent managers thrive while those who do not adapt face displacement.

title: Social and human service assistants
rationale: Core work mixes digital/cognitive tasks (researching benefits, completing paperwork, coordinating services, developing plans) that AI already assists with via case-management tools and resource-matching systems, against heavy interpersonal, empathetic, and in-person client contact that requires physical presence in homes, shelters, or clinics; this keeps disruption moderate. Demand elasticity is moderate-to-high because large unmet needs among aging populations, people with addictions, the homeless, and other vulnerable groups mean cheaper/faster service delivery would expand the volume of clients served rather than simply shrink headcount, though public budgets and regulations constrain unlimited growth. The combination yields a resilient occupation: AI augments peripheral and administrative work without reshaping the human-centered core.

title: Social workers
rationale: Core social work tasks center on in-person assessment, crisis response, relationship-building, home visits, and empathy-driven counseling that require unpredictable real-world presence and human judgment, so AI mainly augments peripheral work such as case notes, resource matching, and treatment planning rather than replacing the occupation’s essence. Demand elasticity is high because large unmet needs exist in mental health, child welfare, substance abuse, and aging support; cheaper and faster delivery would expand access and caseloads rather than simply shrink headcount. With disruption remaining moderate, AI therefore touches the edges without reshaping the core role, producing a resilient occupation.

title: Sociologists
rationale: Sociologists' core duties—designing research, analyzing survey/interview data with statistical tools, synthesizing findings, writing reports, and proposing policies—are predominantly cognitive and language-based, so AI already materially accelerates literature reviews, coding, statistical modeling, and drafting. Some residual human elements remain in fieldwork interviews, observations, and nuanced social interpretation, but these do not prevent high overall disruption. Elasticity is only moderate: cheaper research could unlock more applied work in policy, business, and NGOs, yet academic positions, grant budgets, and institutional demand are structurally constrained and will not expand enough to fully offset productivity gains. The result is restructuring—workers who master AI-augmented methods and focus on theory, fieldwork, and stakeholder translation will thrive, while pure traditional research roles shrink.

title: Software developers, quality assurance analysts, and testers
rationale: Core tasks of coding, designing systems, analyzing requirements, generating tests, and debugging are almost entirely digital and cognitive, already being materially accelerated by AI coding assistants and automated testing tools, placing the occupation squarely in AI's direct path. Demand elasticity is high because software development has historically been cost-constrained; making it dramatically cheaper and faster unlocks substantial latent demand for more applications, features, AI systems, IoT integrations, and custom solutions across industries. This combination means productivity gains expand total output enough to support stable or growing headcount rather than pure contraction, fitting the augment category as each developer/tester produces far more while overall employment continues to rise.

title: Solar photovoltaic installers
rationale: Core tasks center on physical outdoor work—measuring, cutting, assembling support structures, lifting and mounting panels on roofs or ground mounts, wiring connections, and sealing—requiring presence, strength, and manual tool use that AI cannot perform. AI can assist peripheral design optimization, site assessment, or diagnostics, but leaves the hands-on installation largely unchanged over the next decade. Demand is highly elastic because installation cost and speed remain major barriers to solar adoption; productivity gains would unlock substantial latent residential and commercial demand already evident in falling panel prices and policy incentives. With disruption well below the threshold that reshapes the occupation, the net effect is resilient.

title: Special education teachers
rationale: Core duties center on in-person instruction, real-time behavioral and emotional support, physical assistance, and mentoring of students with disabilities—tasks that require human presence and adaptability AI cannot yet perform—while AI already assists knowledge-work elements such as IEP drafting, lesson adaptation, progress analytics, and record-keeping, producing moderate overall disruption. Demand is anchored to the relatively fixed population of identified students with disabilities and is constrained by federal funding mandates, school budgets, and enrollment trends, so productivity gains are unlikely to unlock large new volumes of service. Consequently AI will mainly streamline peripheral and administrative work without displacing the occupation’s essential human core, placing it in the resilient category.

title: Special effects artists and animators
rationale: Core work is almost entirely digital and generative—creating 2D/3D models, CGI, character animation, and VFX in software—so generative AI tools already produce usable assets, in-betweens, backgrounds, and even short sequences, placing the occupation firmly in AI’s direct path. Demand elasticity is high because lower cost and faster turnaround unlock substantial latent volume: more indie games, streaming content, mobile apps, advertising, educational media, and social video that were previously constrained by production budgets. Productivity gains therefore expand total output rather than simply shrinking headcount, allowing skilled artists who direct and refine AI systems to produce far more while overall employment remains stable or grows. This matches the augment category of high disruption paired with high elasticity.

title: Speech-language pathologists
rationale: Core SLP work centers on in-person assessment, real-time interactive therapy (articulation modeling, swallowing exercises, fluency practice), and family counseling that require physical presence, clinical observation, and adaptive human interaction; AI already assists with speech-sample analysis, documentation, and home-practice apps but leaves the bulk of daily client-facing tasks largely unchanged, placing disruption in the moderate range. Demand is currently constrained by shortages, waitlists, school budgets, and cost, so cheaper/faster delivery via AI tools would unlock substantial latent need among children with developmental issues, autism, and an aging population with stroke/dementia-related disorders. Because disruption remains moderate, the occupation is resilient: AI augments peripheral and knowledge tasks without displacing the human-centered core, consistent with projected strong employment growth.

title: Stationary engineers and boiler operators
rationale: Core duties center on physical operation, inspection, repair, and maintenance of boilers, valves, turbines, and HVAC equipment in real facilities, requiring on-site presence, mechanical dexterity, and handling of hazardous conditions that AI cannot perform; AI only peripherally aids sensor monitoring, predictive alerts, and log-keeping. Demand is tightly tied to the fixed stock of large buildings, hospitals, and plants that need utilities, with virtually no latent expansion if the work becomes cheaper or faster. Because disruption remains low, the occupation is resilient regardless of modest efficiency gains.

title: Substance abuse, behavioral disorder, and mental health counselors
rationale: Core tasks center on building therapeutic alliances, crisis intervention, empathy-driven sessions, and in-person work with distressed clients in clinical or residential settings, so AI only assists peripheral elements like documentation, progress tracking, treatment-plan suggestions, and psychoeducation materials rather than replacing the relational core. Demand elasticity is high because mental health and addiction services face massive unmet need, long waitlists, and cost/access barriers; making counseling dramatically cheaper and more productive would unlock far more prevention, mild-case treatment, family support, and ongoing care. The moderate disruption score places the occupation in the resilient category, as AI tools will raise productivity at the margins without reshaping the essential human presence required.

title: Surgical assistants and technologists
rationale: Core duties—sterilizing and arranging instruments, patient positioning and prepping, maintaining sterile fields, passing tools, counting supplies, and hands-on assisting (clamping, suctioning, suturing)—are almost entirely physical, manual, and require real-time presence in the unpredictable OR environment; AI can only touch peripheral tasks such as inventory tracking or robotic-system setup. Demand for surgical procedures is driven by medical necessity, demographics, and facility capacity rather than the marginal cost or speed of technologists, so even large productivity gains unlock only limited additional volume (mainly elective/outpatient cases). Because disruption remains low, the occupation stays resilient regardless of modest elasticity.

title: Survey researchers
rationale: Core tasks—questionnaire design, statistical analysis, sampling adjustments, data summarization, and report writing—are almost entirely digital/cognitive and already partially automated by AI tools for question generation, response coding, and insight extraction, placing the occupation squarely in AI’s path. Elasticity is only moderate because cheaper, faster surveys would unlock more frequent market research and academic polling among cost-sensitive organizations, yet overall demand remains constrained by respondent fatigue, regulatory survey requirements, and substitution from big-data/social-media analytics. High disruption combined with moderate demand expansion therefore implies the role survives but requires substantial skill shifts toward AI oversight, complex methodology, and hybrid data sources.

title: Surveying and mapping technicians
rationale: Core work mixes substantial physical fieldwork (site visits, instrument operation, marker placement, rugged outdoor conditions) with digital tasks (GIS/CAD processing, image editing, data entry, map creation from drone/satellite sources), so AI already assists the knowledge portions via computer vision and automated analysis but cannot replace on-site presence or accuracy verification. Elasticity is moderate because cheaper/faster surveying unlocks more frequent updates, detailed GIS applications, and smaller projects, yet demand remains partly constrained by construction cycles, legal requirements, and infrastructure budgets rather than expanding without limit. With disruption only moderate, AI reshapes tools and efficiency at the periphery without eliminating the occupation's essential human elements, fitting the resilient category.

title: Surveyors
rationale: Surveyors combine physical fieldwork (site measurements with GPS/total stations, terrain navigation) with cognitive/digital tasks (legal record searches, GIS/CAD mapping, data verification, report preparation). AI already assists the latter via automated feature extraction, point-cloud processing, and document analysis, but core on-site presence, equipment operation, legal certification, and court testimony keep disruption moderate. Demand is anchored to construction volume, property transactions, and infrastructure projects rather than surveying cost; cheaper/faster output may unlock some extra mapping or planning work but is constrained by real-world project pipelines and regulation, yielding low elasticity. AI therefore touches supporting tasks without reshaping the occupation’s core, producing a resilient net effect.

title: Tax examiners and collectors, and revenue agents
rationale: Core tasks center on reviewing digital tax returns, applying tax rules to credits/deductions, analyzing financial records, and flagging discrepancies—predominantly cognitive and language-based work already being automated by AI document analysis, anomaly detection, and tax-law models, with only secondary field audits and collections requiring human presence. Demand for enforcement is largely fixed by the volume of returns and government budgets/politics rather than price; while cheaper AI could enable somewhat more audits, latent expansion is capped and productivity gains will primarily shrink headcount rather than scale output proportionally. This combination of high disruption and low elasticity fits replace, as AI absorbs routine examination volume without enough new demand to offset workforce contraction.

title: Taxi drivers, shuttle drivers, and chauffeurs
rationale: Core tasks center on vehicle operation, real-time navigation, and passenger handling in unpredictable traffic and weather; AI already transforms matching/routing via apps and GPS while autonomous vehicles (already deployed in limited markets) are on a clear 10-year trajectory to absorb the driving itself, making disruption high. Demand for rides has some latent upside if costs fall, yet expansion is capped by road capacity, regulation, and the fact that any growth will be met by robotaxis rather than more human drivers. High disruption plus low-moderate elasticity therefore produces net replacement and headcount contraction for the occupation.

title: Teacher assistants
rationale: Teacher assistants spend substantial time on physical presence tasks—supervising recess/lunch/field trips, managing behavior, and providing hands-on support for special-needs students (hygiene, mobility)—so AI can only assist peripheral cognitive pieces such as recordkeeping, material prep, and some one-on-one lesson reinforcement via tutoring software. Demand is constrained by fixed student demographics, public-school budgets, and regulatory staffing ratios; even if AI made assistance far cheaper, schools would not expand headcount dramatically. Because disruption remains moderate, the occupation is resilient: AI augments admin and instructional support without displacing the core human-presence role.

title: Technical writers
rationale: Core tasks—researching products, drafting/editing manuals, FAQs, and multi-modal content, standardizing across platforms—are almost entirely digital, language-based, and cognitive, with current LLMs already generating usable first drafts from specs or code and accelerating revision cycles. Demand expands moderately because cheaper documentation unlocks more thorough coverage, multi-language versions, interactive media, and professional docs for smaller firms and open-source projects, yet overall volume remains tethered to the finite pace of product releases rather than exploding. High disruption plus only moderate elasticity means the occupation persists but shifts toward AI orchestration, domain expertise, usability research, and complex multi-stakeholder coordination; non-adapters face displacement while adapters produce far more output.

title: Telecommunications technicians
rationale: Core work is predominantly physical and site-specific—climbing towers/poles, splicing fiber, installing routers and lines in homes/businesses, and hands-on repairs—making AI largely irrelevant beyond peripheral diagnostics, remote monitoring alerts, predictive maintenance software, and record-keeping. This matches low-disruption trades like electricians. Elasticity is limited because infrastructure demand is constrained by project completion cycles, saturation of connectivity needs, and reduced maintenance for modern fiber/5G systems; cheaper/faster work unlocks only modest expansion in underserved areas rather than transformative volume. Low disruption therefore keeps the occupation resilient overall.

title: Tellers
rationale: Core teller tasks—verifying identities, processing deposits/checks, recording transactions electronically, balancing drawers, and answering routine account questions—are predominantly routine, cognitive, and digital, already being materially automated by online banking, mobile deposits, enhanced ATMs, video kiosks, and AI chatbots, with physical cash handling steadily declining. Demand elasticity is low because the total volume of banking transactions is essentially fixed (or shrinking for in-person channels) and not suppressed by teller cost; customers prefer free self-service digital options rather than consuming more human teller interactions even if they become cheaper. High disruption combined with inelastic demand therefore produces net replacement and headcount contraction, consistent with the already-projected 13% decline.

title: Top executives
rationale: Core tasks center on knowledge work such as analyzing financials and performance data, formulating strategy and policies, and identifying cost or process improvements, all of which AI already assists materially via analytics, scenario modeling, and drafting; leadership, negotiation, and interpersonal accountability still require human presence, keeping disruption high rather than total. Demand elasticity is moderate because organizational hierarchies and the finite number of firms limit how many top roles can exist, yet cheaper/faster executive capacity can unlock better management in smaller firms and more ambitious scaling, producing some expansion without unlimited growth. High disruption paired with only moderate elasticity therefore fits restructure: the occupation persists but the skill mix shifts heavily toward AI orchestration and judgment, displacing those who fail to adapt.

title: Tour and travel guides
rationale: Core tasks center on physical escorting of groups, real-time pacing adjustments, live interpersonal engagement, and handling unpredictable outdoor or site conditions, so AI only meaningfully assists peripheral knowledge work such as research, route planning, and script generation. Demand elasticity is moderate because AI-driven productivity that lowers the cost of high-quality guided experiences can unlock additional leisure travel and niche tours, yet expansion remains bounded by physical site capacity, seasonal constraints, and travelers’ limited free time. With disruption only in the moderate range, AI touches preparation and information delivery without reshaping the occupation’s essential human-presence requirements, placing it firmly in the resilient category.

title: Training and development managers
rationale: Core work is predominantly cognitive and digital—needs assessment, program design, content selection/creation, evaluation, and budget alignment—all of which AI already accelerates via generative content tools, adaptive learning platforms, and analytics, placing the role in the high-disruption band even though people leadership and organizational alignment remain human. Elasticity is high because organizations chronically under-invest in training due to cost and speed constraints; dramatically cheaper, faster, personalized programs unlock large latent demand for continuous reskilling, especially as AI itself reshapes jobs. Productivity gains are therefore absorbed by expanded training volume rather than pure headcount reduction, so the occupation is augmented: managers oversee far more sophisticated systems and larger portfolios of learning.

title: Training and development specialists
rationale: Core work is predominantly knowledge-based—needs assessment, instructional design, content creation for manuals/modules, and program evaluation—all of which AI already accelerates via generative tools, adaptive learning platforms, and analytics, even if live facilitation and interpersonal delivery still require humans. Demand elasticity is high because training has long been under-provided due to cost and time; dramatically cheaper, faster, personalized programs unlock substantial latent corporate demand for continuous upskilling, compliance, and technology-driven reskilling. The combination produces an augment outcome: specialists who leverage AI will each design and deliver far more training while overall headcount grows with expanded organizational investment.

title: Transportation, storage, and distribution managers
rationale: Disruption is high because core duties—planning networks, budgeting, inventory/procurement oversight, performance evaluation, compliance monitoring, and disruption response—are predominantly cognitive, data-driven, and language-based; AI tools already deliver material gains in forecasting, route/inventory optimization, automated reporting, and anomaly detection, with further trajectory toward autonomous decision support. Elasticity is moderate: e-commerce and supply-chain complexity create some latent demand for more sophisticated management, and cheaper tools could extend advanced logistics to smaller firms, yet overall volume of goods movement and physical infrastructure constraints limit expansion, so productivity gains will not fully offset headcount pressure. The combination produces restructure—roles persist but shift heavily toward AI orchestration, exception handling, and strategic oversight, displacing managers who cannot adapt while rewarding those who can.

title: Travel agents
rationale: Travel agents' core tasks—researching fares and options, building itineraries, booking reservations, calculating costs, and advising on destinations/documents—are almost entirely digital, cognitive, and language-based, with AI already generating personalized plans, searching inventories, and handling changes far faster than humans. Physical elements like destination visits are peripheral, so disruption is very high. Elasticity is low because total travel volume is constrained by travelers' time, money, and desire rather than planning friction; cheaper/faster service mainly shifts simple and mid-market bookings to AI tools and platforms instead of expanding overall demand enough to preserve headcount. High disruption combined with low elasticity therefore fits 'replace,' expecting significant contraction as AI absorbs the bulk of the work.

title: Tutors
rationale: Core tutoring tasks—explaining concepts, generating practice problems, providing feedback, and adapting instruction—are predominantly cognitive and language-based, with AI tools already delivering personalized explanations and drills at scale, placing the occupation in the high-disruption range similar to teachers. Demand elasticity is very high because personalized one-on-one instruction has long been cost-prohibitive for most families and lifelong learners; dramatic reductions in price and speed unlock near-unlimited latent demand across K-12, test prep, adult upskilling, and special-needs support. The combination of high disruption with very high elasticity means productivity gains expand total tutoring output rather than shrink headcount, fitting the augment category as AI multiplies the reach of human tutors who focus on motivation, complex adaptation, and relationship-building.

title: Umpires, referees, and other sports officials
rationale: Core work requires physical presence on the field or court, real-time positioning, stamina, split-second human judgment under pressure, and direct interaction with players/coaches, so AI tools (video replay, automated line calls) assist only peripheral decision support rather than reshaping daily tasks. Demand for officials is driven by the fixed volume of games and sports participation rather than the cost or speed of officiating; even if AI made the role dramatically cheaper, the number of events would expand only modestly at amateur levels and not enough to offset productivity gains. Because disruption remains low, the occupation is resilient overall.

title: Urban and regional planners
rationale: Core work is predominantly knowledge-based—data analysis from censuses and studies, GIS modeling, feasibility assessments, report writing, and scenario planning—all of which AI already accelerates via automated mapping, predictive simulations, generative design, and document drafting, even as stakeholder meetings, public hearings, and site inspections retain human requirements. Demand elasticity is moderate because cheaper, faster planning unlocks more detailed climate/housing/transportation studies and better coverage for smaller jurisdictions or private consulting, yet total volume remains constrained by fixed numbers of local governments, political processes, and public budgets rather than expanding unboundedly. This produces a restructure outcome: the occupation persists with substantially shifted skills toward AI orchestration and community facilitation, displacing those who do not adapt while elevating those who do.

title: Veterinarians
rationale: Core veterinary work centers on physical examination, wound treatment, surgery, vaccination, and handling unpredictable animals, all of which require real-world presence and manual dexterity; AI already assists with imaging analysis, differential diagnosis suggestions, and client communication but leaves the hands-on majority of tasks intact, placing disruption firmly in the moderate range. Demand elasticity is moderate because lower costs and faster throughput would unlock additional preventive visits, advanced procedures for cost-sensitive owners, and expanded livestock/wildlife coverage, yet overall volume remains constrained by the finite pet and farm-animal population and the time still required for physical procedures. With disruption at or below 6, the occupation is resilient: AI augments peripheral knowledge work without reshaping the essential in-person clinical role.

title: Veterinary assistants and laboratory animal caretakers
rationale: Core duties—feeding, bathing, restraining, cleaning cages, sterilizing instruments, and physically assisting with procedures—are almost entirely hands-on and require real-world presence with unpredictable animals, so AI can only touch peripheral admin or monitoring tasks. Demand elasticity is moderate because lower costs could modestly expand pet procedures and research animal use as spending barriers fall, yet overall volume remains constrained by pet ownership rates and research needs rather than exploding. With disruption well below the threshold that reshapes the occupation, the role stays resilient: AI augments edges without displacing or fundamentally altering the physical work.

title: Veterinary technologists and technicians
rationale: Core tasks center on physical animal handling—restraining, bathing, administering anesthesia/meds, surgery prep, and hands-on nursing—which require real-world presence, manual dexterity, and strength that AI cannot perform; AI only assists peripheral elements like lab/x-ray interpretation, case-history documentation, and monitoring alerts. Demand elasticity is moderate because pet ownership and discretionary spending are already rising and lower costs would unlock more frequent visits, preventive care, and treatments for price-sensitive owners, yet physical bottlenecks and clinic capacity limit unbounded expansion. The net effect is resilient since disruption remains moderate (well below the high-disruption threshold), so AI reshapes support tools without displacing the occupation’s essential hands-on role.

title: Waiters and waitresses
rationale: Core tasks are overwhelmingly physical and presence-based—carrying trays, clearing tables, standing/walking for hours, and real-time customer interaction in unpredictable dining environments—with only peripheral language or digital elements (order taking, POS entry, menu explanations) that AI or kiosks can already partially handle. AI tools today and near-term robots do not meaningfully reshape the hands-on service work, keeping disruption low. Demand for table service is largely fixed by meal frequency, restaurant capacity, and dining habits; even large productivity gains from automation translate mostly into fewer servers per cover rather than dramatically more full-service dining, producing low elasticity. The combination yields a resilient occupation where AI remains peripheral.

title: Water and wastewater treatment plant and system operators
rationale: Core work mixes physical presence (equipment inspection, chemical addition, sample collection, cleaning, emergency manual overrides, and outdoor maintenance) with computerized monitoring and data logging; AI already aids process optimization, anomaly detection, and reporting but cannot replace hands-on mechanical and safety tasks, placing disruption in the moderate range. Demand for treated water and wastewater processing is set by population, industrial activity, and regulation rather than operator cost or speed, so productivity gains translate almost directly into fewer workers rather than expanded volume. Because disruption stays at or below 6, the occupation remains resilient overall even as automation continues to trim headcount.

title: Water transportation workers
rationale: Core tasks center on physical vessel operation, engine maintenance, deck work, and real-time navigation in unpredictable sea conditions requiring human presence, manual dexterity, and local knowledge; AI assists with route optimization, predictive maintenance, and monitoring but leaves the hands-on and on-board duties largely unchanged over the next decade. Demand for water transport is driven by commodity trade volumes, passenger needs, and infrastructure constraints rather than being heavily cost-suppressed, so even large productivity gains would produce only modest expansion in shipping or ferry activity. Because disruption remains low, the occupation stays resilient with AI confined to peripheral tools rather than reshaping daily work or headcount.

title: Web developers and digital designers
rationale: Core tasks—coding in HTML/JS, layout design, prototyping, graphics integration, and testing—are almost entirely digital and cognitive, already heavily assisted by AI tools like code generators, design copilots, and site builders, placing the occupation firmly in the very-high disruption range. Demand elasticity is high because lower cost and faster production unlock substantial latent demand: more small businesses, e-commerce experiments, mobile interfaces, and frequent redesigns become viable, expanding total output rather than merely shrinking headcount. This combination of high disruption with high elasticity produces an augment outcome in which each worker produces far more while overall employment remains stable or grows.

title: Welders, cutters, solderers, and brazers
rationale: Core tasks are overwhelmingly physical and manual—operating torches and equipment in awkward positions, lifting metal, and adapting to unique on-site conditions—which AI and robotics can only partially automate outside highly repetitive factory settings; AI assists mainly with peripheral blueprint interpretation, parameter optimization, or visual inspection. Demand elasticity is low because welding volume is constrained by material costs, construction/infrastructure needs, and overall manufacturing output rather than welding labor cost alone, so large productivity gains translate mostly into fewer workers rather than dramatically more welded products. With disruption well below the high threshold, the occupation remains resilient: AI touches edges but does not reshape the hands-on core work over the next decade.

title: Wholesale and manufacturing sales representatives
rationale: Core tasks center on prospecting, product explanation, negotiation, contract prep, and sales analysis—predominantly cognitive and language-based work where AI tools (lead scoring, generative pitches, CRM automation, chatbots) already deliver material productivity gains, even as outside sales retains some travel and relationship elements. Elasticity is moderate because lower sales costs unlock more outreach and market penetration for manufacturers and wholesalers, yet overall goods demand, online self-service channels, and competitive saturation prevent unlimited expansion. This produces a restructure outcome: the occupation persists but shifts heavily toward AI-augmented complex-deal and relationship skills, displacing those who cannot adapt.

title: Wind turbine technicians
rationale: Core tasks center on physical presence—climbing 200+ ft towers, confined-space mechanical/electrical/hydraulic repairs, blade work, and heavy-tool handling in outdoor/offshore conditions—so AI remains peripheral (predictive diagnostics, remote monitoring, data analysis, drone inspections). These tools already assist but do not displace the hands-on work, keeping disruption low. Elasticity is moderate because cheaper, faster maintenance lowers wind LCOE and can accelerate turbine deployment amid energy-transition demand, yet growth is still gated by capital construction, siting, and policy rather than unlimited latent service demand. Net effect is therefore resilient: AI augments efficiency at the margin without reshaping the occupation’s physical core.

title: Woodworkers
rationale: Core woodworking tasks—lifting materials, operating saws/mills/sanders, hand-tool assembly, finishing, and machine maintenance—are predominantly physical and require real-world presence, so AI only peripherally assists via design optimization, CNC programming, or vision-based inspection. Demand for furniture, cabinets, and wood products is constrained by housing stock, renovation cycles, and space rather than pure cost, so even large productivity gains produce limited volume expansion and tend to shrink headcount, consistent with existing automation trends. Because disruption remains low-to-moderate, the occupation is resilient: AI does not reshape the essential hands-on work.

title: Writers and authors
rationale: Core tasks of writers and authors—researching, drafting, revising, and producing language-based content for books, ads, scripts, blogs, and more—are almost entirely digital and cognitive, placing them squarely in AI's path; generative models already produce usable drafts and outlines that materially change daily workflows. Demand elasticity is high because content production has long been constrained by cost and time: dramatically cheaper writing unlocks far more marketing copy, self-published books, personalized content, scripts, and online material that businesses and individuals previously forwent. Productivity gains are therefore absorbed by expanded total output rather than pure headcount reduction, allowing adaptable writers who leverage AI to produce substantially more. This combination of high disruption and high elasticity fits the augment category.

title: Zoologists and wildlife biologists
rationale: Core duties center on fieldwork, specimen collection, animal handling, and on-site observation in remote or unpredictable habitats, which remain physical and presence-dependent; AI already aids modeling, GIS analysis, population estimation, and report writing but does not displace these foundational tasks, yielding only moderate disruption. Demand is largely government- and grant-funded with structural budget ceilings, so productivity gains from cheaper analysis or monitoring expand output only modestly rather than unlocking large latent markets. Because disruption stays at or below the moderate threshold, the occupation is resilient: AI touches analytical edges without reshaping the essential human role in wildlife study and conservation.
